dedupe_keys.name: toolbox for transboundary water contingency management in the sava river basin climate adapt case study

description: This Climate-ADAPT case study describes a toolbox for transboundary water contingency management that the International Sava River Basin Commission had developed in the WACOM project between July 2020 and December 2022. It has three parts: a real-time knowledge sharing platform to coordinate responses to transboundary accidents, a GIS-based model of the whole basin showing real-time and hypothetical flooding and pollution, and a catalogue of best practices. Development cost just over 2.9 million euros from the Interreg Danube programme and other EU funds; the commission put the modelling tool into use in 2023. Coverage is the Sava basin in Slovenia, Croatia, Bosnia and Herzegovina and Serbia. The page is accessible online as free HTML on the Climate-ADAPT portal, published in 2024 and updated in 2026. Caveats: the coordination tool was still being implemented in 2024, and its use depends on cooperation across borders. Simulation uses: basin-scale flood and pollution scenarios for emergency response planning. Related records: the Prague flood protection case study (case_study-prague-vltava-flood-protection-system).
name: Toolbox for transboundary water contingency management in the Sava River Basin (Climate-ADAPT case study)
outcomes: Agencies trained on the toolbox used it for flood preparedness and response in the 2023 floods in Slovenia and confirmed its value.
resources_used: GIS-based basin model of real-time and hypothetical flooding and pollution
